cards.note:
Cilaos is a town in central Reunion which is easy to identify. It is located inside a caldera and has mountains surrounding it on all sides. All coverage is also overcast or rainy.

If you are in a town you are probably in Cilaos itself. If you think you are in the caldera but are on a mountain road, you are very likely to be on a road either south or east of Cilaos.

This is an easily identifiable section of the N2 on the East coast of the island. Parts of it have lots of vegetation either side of the road. Other parts have been impacted by volcanic eruptions and have no grass and emerging plants. These volcano-affected sections are actually visible on the map which can make pinpointing possible.

Green bus stops are found in the north region (named Saint-Denis) and are often found alongside a yellow bus stop. Almost all coverage in this region is either on or north of the N2 (or the N6 once you reach Sainte-Clotilde). The Saint-Denis/Sainte-Clotilde area has the majority of the region's non-highway coverage.

The bus stops found in the west region (named Saint-Paul) are different to the rest of the island. Some are shaped like an upside-down L and some are blocky bus shelters. These can either be white or a grey-green. Only main roads are covered in this region (besides a few coastal towns) and you can often get a good guess by factoring in how high up the mountain you are.

Cilaos is a town in central Reunion which is inside a caldera and has mountains surrounding it on all sides. All coverage is also overcast or rainy. If you think you are in the caldera but are on a mountain road, you are very likely to be on a road either south or east of Cilaos.

Most of this coverage is in the top half of the D242 (ending in Ilet A Cordes) and the N5 from Cilaos down to Le Pavillon. A very small portion on the D241 in the north of Cilaos also has coverage.

This is an easily identifiable part of the N1 on the North coast of the island which follows the N1 from La Possession to where it ends just outside of Saint-Denis. There are steep cliffs and a single concrete divider separating the opposite lanes most of the way.

It is important to note that Le Port and La Possession have no coverage apart from the N1, so if you are on a north-facing road that isn't this one, you are likely further east than further south.

Orange bus stops are found in the east region (named Saint-Benoit) and are often found alongside a yellow bus stop. All coverage in this region is either on the N2 or the N3, both of which are fully covered (half of the D54 in Saint-Benoit is also covered but it is rare).

Pink bus stops are found in the south region (named Saint-Pierre). They are almost the only bus stop found on or west of the N5 including the area around Cilaos. They can also rarely be found in Saint-Pierre and the N3 but nowhere outside that. The only roads north of the D11 which have coverage are the D16, D20, and N5 up to Cilaos which can further help region guessing.

Red bus stops are sometimes found on the west coast in the Region of Saint-Paul. These span from the town of Saint-Gilles down to Saint-Leu where they stop. These are the rarest bus stop on the island so if you find one, your region guess will be very good.

The Route du Volcan (RF5) is an easily identifiable road in the south-eastern part of the island. The soil and road is noticeably red and there is very little vegetation besides shrubs. White stones also line the side of the road.

The road starts in the village of Bourg-Murat but the road only becomes truly identifiable once you are out of the village.

The RF58 is an easily identifiable road connected to the D20, south-west of Cilaos. It is one of the only dirt paths with official coverage and has very dense vegetation (notably pine and eucalyptus trees). The vehicle-made 2 tyre lanes become more visible the further up the road you are.

If you are on a paved road with similar vegetation you are likely on the D20 instead (in the area where it connects to the RF58)

Saint-Paul and Saint-Denis are the two most covered towns in Reunion. One easy way to differentiate them is their bollards often found at street intersections. Saint-Paul uses black bollards whereas Saint-Denis uses green bollards (both are occasionally painted white on the top part). Similar bollards are occasionally seen elsewhere so checking for the coast direction is advised.

Sugarcane Plantations are found along the North East and South West coast of Reunion. When you see these, check where the coast and/or the mountains are in relation to where you are, and you can quickly know which of the 2 sections of the island you are on. Combine with other clues if you can find any!

Yellow bus stops are mostly found on their own in the island's south region of Saint-Pierre. This includes the northern half of the N3 as well as the entire N2. Nowhere except Saint-Joseph and the N2 is covered east of the town of Saint-Pierre. Use the angle of the coast (or the lack of coast) to get a great region guess.

However, make sure to check it cannot be elsewhere in Reunion. Yellow bus stops can be found scattered around the island's main roads in other regions so check for other clues if you can.
